verdict.rationale: Paperspace documents Notebooks as a web-based Jupyter IDE and says users can connect to remote Jupyter kernels through alternative IDEs. Machines support SSH connections, which covers the core of opening Jupyter or attaching an IDE. However, nothing documents a one-step VS Code or Cursor connection, and one hands-on user reported that getting SSH access to Core machines was 'an uphill battle', which lowers confidence in how seamless this is. Missing for 10: documented one-step VS Code/Cursor integration, detail on the alternative-IDE kernel connection flow, independent corroboration of smooth IDE/Jupyter access.

support.subject: As a developer, I can open Jupyter or connect my IDE (VS Code/Cursor) to the instance in one step

citations.quote: Notebooks are a web-based Jupyter IDE with shared persistent storage for long-term development and inter-notebook collaboration, backed by accelerated compute.
Connect to remote Jupyter kernels through alternative IDEs.
You can connect to your Linux or Windows-based machine using the Paperspace console or desktop app using SSH connection.
